log.msg: THE PLAN'S SLICE 2 CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN, and three of its five steps are why. (1) blocks.js cannot re-export core's five word lists: slice 1 moved the six words, the classes and the frame into core but NOT the lists, and my fence lets me touch core only for the four corrections - so there is nothing to re-export from, and pointing blocks.js at an empty seam would break imagine/sections/sections.js, which imports SURFACES straight out of it. (2) stage.js cannot delete the sixteen methods and inherit: core's PageFrame draws a REAL page (children are Pages, a row is an anchor with an href, a click is a Router navigation, this.page IS the page) while PagingStage draws a DEMO of a page (children are four made-up objects, a click swaps a panel in memory and changes no address, this.page is the OWNING page, and the caption measures the box before and after so it can report pixels). Same boxes, different machine; every one of the sixteen would have to be written again the next line down. (3) make/page.js grow() cannot become Page.from(): Page.from() FETCHES a page.json at a url, grow() walks the tree Make already holds in memory and hangs node_now(), delete_now() and a WRITING content() on each node. Step 5 (build/stage.js keeps crumbs, title and the child panel and inherits the rest) was already true before I started - the file is 115 lines and says so in its own header.

WHAT I DID INSTEAD, and it is the half of the slice that is real: the lab became a CONSUMER of everything core actually took. PagingStage extends Page.Frame (so it wears .paging-stage.page-frame and core's skeleton), and the stage, the toolbar's colour dot, a Paging page that wears a surface and the navigation lab all say core's class names now - page-surface-*, page-type-*, page-nav-reserve, page-nav-hidden, page-frame-body, page-frame-mid. paging.css deleted its own copies of all four.

CORRECTION 1 PROVEN LIVE at 1280 (headless evaluate, not read): a Page saying only surface: card renders as "page flow page--card standard" - no page-surface-* on the page - and its box renders as "page-canvas page-surface-card". One border (page 0px, box 1px) and one background (page transparent, box white). The frame is still built for a page whose ONLY word is surface, because render() asks the new words_said() rather than word_classes().length.

CORRECTION 3 PROVEN LIVE: a page in a columns row whose content is "/framework/core/Page/doc/columns.md" now draws the file. column() calls render_content() - the same reader render() uses - and the column prose reads "Columns - a page whose subtree is a row. One call, and every page under this one is a full-height column...". It printed the address as a line of text before.

CORRECTION 4: the SWAPS comment in Frame.js now says LEAVE IT OUT and why - ext/tabs brings its own panel and fills the same regions Map, so listing tabs there reserves a second panel and draws the child twice - plus the one line that explains why the lab's own list DOES include tabs (the lab draws its own strip).

CORRECTION 2 PROVEN BY SCRIPT, and the script is the answer to "say how you checked": every class token in every selector of paging.css, navigation.css and baseline.css, checked against every .js/.md/.json file under public/ for a literal or for a concatenation prefix ("paging-rail paging-rail-" + side counts). Result: paging.css 171 classes, 0 with no emitter; navigation.css 62, 0; baseline.css 8, 0; core Page.css 79, 0. Two were flagged on the first run - paging-rail-right, a false positive the prefix reader now handles, and .paging-panel, a genuinely dead 8-line rule nothing had emitted since the expand rows became .paging-held. Deleted.

log.msg: THE NINE-STEP USE TEST, ALL NINE PASS, every step screenshotted (scratchpad graduate-2/nine/). (1) PICK - the four dropdowns and the address field took navigation=Left rail, room=Reading, page colour=Dark and CONTENT = a .md file I wrote an hour earlier. (2) SEND - ?navigation=rail&content=%2Fframework%2Fai%2F2026-09-06%2Fgraduate-2%2Fnote.md&room=reading&page-colour=dark. (3) OPEN COLD - a fresh browser at that address gave all seven dropdown values back, identical. (6) CONTENT YOU WROTE - the box holds my note, which did not exist when this realm was written. (4)+(5)+(8) SAVE + NEST + SAVE THE NEST in one press: nest field dashboard, name Slice two proof, Make this a page - made/slice-two-proof/page.json holds all seven words AND nest dashboard, and the parent gained the name. (7) EDIT FROM THE PAGE'S OWN BAR - on /make/slice-two-proof/ I set ROOM to Full and the file read room full within the second, with the nest kept. (9) DELETE - the page's own drawer offered Delete Slice two proof, then Yes; the file is gone, the parent no longer names it, and the url answers 404. made/ is byte-identical to the baseline by md5 (6 files, all six hashes unchanged).

ONE TEST-HARNESS TRAP WORTH THE LINE, because it looked exactly like a product bug: the realm's front page is built at boot and merely hidden, so ITS toolbar and ITS drawer are still in the DOM. A querySelector that does not ask what is on SCREEN drives the wrong page's dropdown - step 7 read room=reading off the file and step 9 could not find the Delete control, on a page whose own bar was working perfectly. Filtering to elements with a client rect passed both immediately. A human clicks what they can see; a script has to be told to.

THE CRAWL, BEFORE AND AFTER: the same 109 urls (identical list), 5 console messages before and 5 after, ZERO new and zero gone - all five are the known declared-child probe 404 on imagine/paging/readme/page.js, one at each of the four widths plus one during discovery. No page timed out in either run.

THE PIXEL DIFFS ARE CONFOUNDED, AND I CAN PROVE BOTH HALVES OF THAT. Before/after on the six control surfaces reads 18k-403k pixels, which would be alarming if it were mine. It is not: four other minions landed app.js, core/Search, core/Layout, ext/demo and styles/layouts in the 30 minutes between my two runs (git status and file mtimes), and app.js is on every page. The brief said to expect them and not to measure them. TWO CONTROLS SEPARATE THE TWO CAUSES. (a) Determinism: the same code shot twice, minutes apart, differs by 0 on every one of the six surfaces except /framework/, whose live clock differs by 1901 px at 1280 and 2635 at 3440 in exactly the box slice 1 named. (b) History: the crawl shoots the controls after 109 realm pages in one context, and a fresh context shooting the same six differs by 0 - so SPA state is not a factor either.

SO I ISOLATED MY OWN CHANGE INSTEAD, and this is the number that matters. On the CURRENT code, twelve realm pages shot twice at each of four widths - once as they are, once with the lab's three old declarations forced back on (the only three that were not character-identical to core's). At 400: 0 px on all twelve. At 1280: 0 px on eleven of twelve; /cross/ reflows one column of text by 15,781 px. At 1920 and 3440: six pages move, and the whole of the movement is the stage's inner gaps finally ramping with the rest of the site - calc(var(--gap-ramp) * 0.6) is 14px at 1920 and 25px at 3440 where the lab's hand-written 0.6em was 10px everywhere. That flat em was the last holdout from before the spacing pass.

AND THE ISOLATION FOUND A REAL BREAK BEFORE ANYONE ELSE DID. Core's frame stacks its rail, box and panel below 34em - right for a page you read on a phone, wrong for a 208px cell whose whole job is to show a rail BESIDE a box. At 1280 on /imagine/paging/cross/, every LEFT RAIL and RIGHT RAIL cell of the 49 drew its rail with the box wrapped underneath and clipped away by the 13em crop: 95,341 px, the shape the wall exists to show being the one thing missing. One rule fixes it - .paging-shot-frame .page-frame-body { container-type: normal } - because a container query with no container to ask never fires. 95,341 px down to 15,781, and the wall looks like it did this morning.

LINE COUNTS, HONESTLY. git diff --stat under imagine/paging/ reads 130 insertions and 84 deletions across 14 files, against the plan's ~500 deleted - a gap of about 83%, and the log line above explains where 470 of those lines went: they are not duplicates, they are the demo instrument. Of the 84 deleted, 50 are CSS declarations or selectors (34 of them in paging.css) and the rest are the comments that stood over them; of the 130 added, the great majority are the comments that now say WHERE each deleted rule went and WHY the two that stayed did. Core moved 45 insertions / 16 deletions across three files for the four corrections. The deletion that WAS available and is real: five duplicated rule blocks and one dead rule, and one class - PagingStage - that now inherits core's frame instead of describing it again.

assign.outcome:
**The paging lab is a reader of core's words now — and half of slice 2 turned out not to be a copy at all.**

The lab deleted every rule core actually took and imports the rest: `PagingStage extends Page.Frame`, so the stage wears `.paging-stage.page-frame` and core's skeleton, and the five surface words, the three type steps and the height reservation are core's CSS. One dead rule went with them. **84 lines deleted, 130 added under [`/imagine/paging/`](/imagine/paging/)** — against the plan's ~500, and the gap is the finding: three of slice 2's five steps cannot be run as written.

![the page I made during the nine-step test, before deleting it](nine-step.png)

**The four corrections, each proven live rather than read**

- `surface` paints the box only — a page saying `surface: card` renders `page flow page--card standard` and its box renders `page-canvas page-surface-card`. One border, one background, no card inside a card.
- No orphan selectors — every class in `paging.css` (171), `navigation.css` (62) and `baseline.css` (8) is emitted by some file. `.paging-panel` was genuinely dead; deleted.
- `content` as a url works in a columns row — `column()` calls the same `render_content()` as `render()`; it printed the address as text before.
- `tabs` stays out of the frame's SWAPS list, with the reason written at the spot.

**Why the other half could not be done, and it is not effort.** Core's `Page.Frame` draws a *real* page — children are `Page`s, a row is an `<a href>`, a click is a Router navigation. `PagingStage` draws a *demo* of one — children are made-up objects, a click swaps a panel in memory, and the caption measures the box before and after to report the pixels. Same boxes, different machine, so the sixteen methods cannot be deleted into it. `blocks.js` cannot re-export core's word lists because core took the words and not the lists. `grow()` cannot become `Page.from()` because it walks a tree Make already holds in memory and hangs the editor on it. All three are written up in [decisions](/imagine/paging/doc/decisions/).

**Proof.** 109 urls × 400/1280/1920/3440, before and after: the same list, the same five console messages, **zero new**. The nine-step use test: **all nine pass**, every step shot, the page deleted by the feature under test, `made/` byte-identical by md5. The six control surfaces are **confounded** — four other minions landed `app.js`, `core/Search`, `core/Layout` and `ext/demo` between my two runs — so I isolated my own change instead: **0 px on eleven of twelve realm pages at 400 and 1280**; at 1920/3440 the stage's gaps finally ramp with the rest of the site. That isolation caught a real break first: core's frame stacked the rail below 34em inside the 208px cells of [Cross](/imagine/paging/cross/), hiding the shape the wall exists to show. One rule fixes it.

**Left, deliberately** — the five word lists stay in `blocks.js` (core has nowhere to put them and my fence forbade making one; slice 3 should fold `imagine/layouts`'s third copy in here). `.paging-bg-*` and `.paging-room-*` stay in the lab: three of the five page colours and all four room words mean something different on a demo frame than on a page, and each says so beside itself. And one line for the `ui-test` skill went unwritten — `.claude/` is outside my fence: **filter to visible elements**, because this realm's front page is built at boot and merely hidden, so its toolbar and drawer are still in the DOM and a blind selector drives the wrong page's dropdown.
